story: Aanya is excited to start school, and her family helps her speak to the school when she needs a place in class.
explain: This is the right to education: every child should have a chance to learn. This is protected by the Right to Education Act.

story: Kabir gets a message from someone he does not know that makes him uneasy. He stops replying and tells his aunt.
options: Right to be safe from harm
answer: Right to be safe from harm
explain: This is the right to be safe from harm. Telling a trusted adult is a strong step; online safety is supported by the Information Technology Act.

story: Meera has time after school to rest, play badminton, and spend time with her friends.
explain: This is the right to play and rest. The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child says children need time to grow, play, and recharge.

story: Arjun shares his ideas when his school asks students how to make the library more welcoming.
options: Right to be safe from harm
explain: This is the right to be heard: children can share their views about things that affect them. This is supported by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

story: Zoya feels unwell at school, so she tells her teacher and visits the school nurse with help from a trusted adult.
explain: This is the right to health: children deserve care when they are unwell. This is supported by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

story: Imran notices that his name is spelled incorrectly on a school form, and a teacher helps make sure it is written correctly.
options: Right to be safe from harm
explain: This is the right to identity: every child has a name and belongs. This is supported by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

story: Tara uses a wheelchair, and her class plans an activity so she can join in with everyone else.
explain: This is the right to be included: every child should be welcomed and supported. The Right to Education Act supports inclusive learning.

story: Dev is worried because older children keep asking him to work instead of going to class. He tells his teacher, who helps him find support.
options: Right to be safe from harm
answer: Right to be safe from harm
explain: This is the right to be safe from harm and to keep learning. The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act helps protect children from harmful work.
